t: This is Onslow Square, a garden square in South Kensington. Several people of note were connected with it. Herbert Ryle was born here in 1856. He became an Old Testament scholar and Anglican bishop, serving as Bishop of Exeter, then Winchester, and finally Dean of Westminster. Florence Pomeroy, Viscountess Harberton, a campaigner for dress reform, died here in 1911. So did Sir Geoffrey Agnew, chairman of the family firm of art dealers Thomas Agnew and Sons, who was called the dean of London art dealers.
